sections.h2: Putnam County Register of Deeds: location and role
sections.html:
The office is in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse, 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the phone is 931-526-7101.

Staff record land deeds, mortgages, releases, plats, powers of attorney and liens, including judgment liens, materialman's liens and state and federal tax liens. The records go back to 1854, the year Putnam County was re-established after courts dissolved an earlier version of it. Anyone can request a copy of a recorded document in person, by phone, by mail or by email. The exception is military discharge papers (DD-214), which are not public.

Employees will help you work out a fee, but they cannot draft a deed for you. When you sell a Putnam County house, a title company or attorney usually prepares the deed, and the register records it once the tax is paid.

Fees for deeds and trust deeds are charged by the thousand dollars, with per-page and flat charges added. A $2.00 fee applies to anything filed electronically, in place since July 1, 2023.

Putnam County recording fees by document type
Document typeFee charged by the county
Warranty deed$3.70 per thousand, $5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $1.00 clerk fee, $2.00 EDP fee
Trust deed (mortgage)$1.15 per thousand after the first $2,000, plus the same page, clerk and EDP fees
ModificationCharged like a trust deed, with no $2,000 deduction
Release$10.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $5.00 for each extra reference
Other documents$5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $5.00 for each added page, plus $2.00 EDP fee
Fixture filing$13.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $15.00 for each added name
DD-214 dischargeFree

Page counts move the total, so call 931-526-7101 if your paperwork comes with odd attachments.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Putnam County home sale?
sections.html:
Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100. The state Department of Revenue treats the purchase price as the base, and its help desk adds that the tax generally uses the greater of the price paid or the property's value, under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. The county's warranty deed line of $3.70 per thousand is the same rate written another way.

A buyer who finances also pays the indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000, collected when the trust deed is recorded. Flat page, clerk and EDP fees come on top of both taxes.

The purchase contract and your title agent decide who carries each charge. Ask for a written estimate of both taxes and the recording fees before the closing date, so nothing changes at the table.

sections.h2: What a document needs to be recorded
sections.html:
The register lists seven requirements, and a document that misses one will not be accepted at the counter.

  • It must be the original or a certified copy.
  • It must state who prepared it.
  • The grantor and grantee must be named.
  • The date of signing must appear.
  • A deed must carry an Oath of Consideration.
  • A deed of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.
  • A notary statement and notary seal must be present.

The oath matters because the tax is based on it. Fill in the real price or value, and let the title agent review the figure before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Researching a property and guarding against deed fraud
sections.html:
You can search records in person at the courthouse, or online through US Title Search, which charges a monthly fee. The office can also look up the year a house was built from its tax card, and the Assessor's Office holds the same detail.

The register promotes My Land Alert, a free service at mylandalert.com that sends an email when a document is recorded in your name or your business name. Owners who rent out a house or live elsewhere should consider it. An alert gives you days, not years, to spot a deed you did not sign.

sections.h2: How do you change or correct a deed?
sections.html:
A recorded deed cannot be edited at the counter. To add or remove a name, you need a new deed prepared by an attorney or title agency, then recorded with the proper oath and fees.

Owners may write their own deed, but the register does not recommend it and cannot help prepare one. A homemade deed that omits a required line gets turned away, and that can hold up a closing. When a mortgage is paid off, the lender sends the release to the register, and you can ask for a copy once it is recorded.

sections.h2: Steps for recording a deed when you sell
sections.html:
A sale in Cookeville, Algood, Baxter, Monterey or anywhere else in the county goes to the same courthouse office. Here is how the visit usually plays out.

  1. The title company or attorney prepares the deed with the grantor, grantee, preparer, date, Oath of Consideration and notary block.
  2. The sale price or value on the oath is reviewed so the transfer tax is figured correctly.
  3. The deed arrives as an original or certified copy, along with payment of the tax and recording fees.
  4. If a mortgage is being paid off, the lender sends its release separately, and a new buyer loan brings its own trust deed.
  5. After recording, ask for a copy of what was filed and keep it with your closing papers.

A cash sale that closes as-is often leaves the deed as the only document at the register, so the recording step is quick when the paperwork is complete.

Putnam County covers 403 square miles and runs on Central Time. Cookeville is the county seat and the largest city. The Census estimate is 86,612 people on July 1, 2025, up 8.4 percent from the 2020 base. The county has 38,375 housing units and a 61.2 percent owner-occupancy rate, with median rent of $908 and median household income of $58,912. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,450, and owners without one report $446.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a warranty deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: The county charges $3.70 per thousand dollars of value, $5.00 per page with a two-page minimum, a $1.00 clerk fee and a $2.00 EDP fee. Call 931-526-7101 for a total on your document.

faqs.q: Who handles deed recording and where is the office?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds is in Room 3 of the Putnam County Courthouse, 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501. The number is 931-526-7101.

faqs.q: Do I need an Oath of Consideration to record a deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Yes. Deeds must include an Oath of Consideration, and deeds of trust must state the maximum principal indebtedness.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of someone else's deed in Putnam County?
faqs.a: Yes. Every recorded document is public except DD-214 discharge papers, and you can request copies in person, by phone, by mail or by email.

faqs.q: Can I add or remove a name on my Putnam County deed myself?
faqs.a: A new deed is required, and an attorney or title agency should prepare it. The office cannot help write the deed and does not recommend doing it yourself.
